teaching_promise: The viewer can trace a learned artifact from a versioned threat model through separate attack lanes, adaptive evaluation, utility and recovery ledgers, and a bounded handoff without mistaking one robustness score for secure deployment.

story.concrete_case: A public toy model is probed by evasion, poisoning, backdoor, extraction, inversion, transfer, multimodal, and agentic attack lanes under a frozen model-threat record; a defense must face an adaptive attacker and keep clean utility, recovery, latency, and residual cost visible.
story.opening_question: What exactly is being defended when the model, checkpoint, attacker, budget, modality, and lifecycle stage all change?
story.payoff: A model-threat ledger separates the lanes, records the denominator and effect, and hands off only a bounded result with no automatic transfer to frontier models or production.
story.transfer: Carry the attack-surface ledger into Privacy, Data Rights, and Information-Flow Governance, where authorized access can still violate purpose, minimization, retention, or rights.

art_direction.visual_thesis: Model security is a versioned, adaptive threat contract with separate attack lanes, not a single robustness badge.
art_direction.signature_image: A dark attack-surface lab keeps one checkpoint in the center while colored lanes for evasion, poisoning, backdoor, extraction, inversion, transfer, multimodal, and agentic attacks remain separately counted.
art_direction.visual_world: A security-lab desk with a checkpoint vault, threat-contract header, attack-lane matrix, adaptive defense arena, utility/recovery ledger, and bounded handoff airlock.
art_direction.composition_rule: Keep model/checkpoint center, threat identity above, attack lanes left and below, defense and utility ledger right, and evidence ceiling/handoff anchored at the bottom.
art_direction.palette_rule: Blue marks model identity and evidence, amber marks threat contract and budgets, red marks attacks or residuals, violet marks adaptive defense, green marks clean utility or admitted control, and gray marks unresolved scope; every color is labeled.
art_direction.typography_rule: Use compact uppercase labels for checkpoint, lifecycle, attacker knowledge, budget, lane, utility, recovery, and residual; narration explains the security meaning.
art_direction.motion_character: Threat fields bind, attack lanes split, adaptive attackers move around defenses, utility counters trade off, and bounded evidence passes through an airlock.
art_direction.camera_rule: Widen from the checkpoint to the full lane matrix, tighten on adaptive attack and denominator accounting, then return to the bounded evidence airlock.
art_direction.surface_rule: Every panel names a model identity, threat field, attack lane, denominator, defense, utility, recovery, cost, residual, or support boundary; omitted capabilities remain outside scope.
art_direction.ending_image: The model-threat receipt seals a finite local result while a privacy and rights ledger opens beyond the airlock.

audio_direction.narration_style: Concrete, calm, and attack-surface precise; the checkpoint ledger carries the causal arc.
audio_direction.pacing_arc: Open with the attack surface, reject robustness proxies, construct the threat contract and separate lanes, trace adaptive evaluation and failures, then narrow the evidence and hand off.
audio_direction.duration_rationale: The 04:31.570 runtime stays below the six-minute soft target while preserving model identity, attack lanes, adaptive controls, utility, recovery, evidence, and handoff; six minutes is a soft target, not a hard cap.
audio_direction.music_policy: No music; lane separation, adaptive motion, and airlock closure carry the rhythm.
audio_direction.sound_effect_policy: No sound effects; labels, counters, arrows, crosses, and containment encode meaning.

accessibility.color_redundancy: Every lane and outcome uses labels, enclosure, position, arrow direction, line style, or crosses in addition to color.
accessibility.motion_redundancy: Every attack lane settles into a named state; the utility ledger and airlock remain legible when motion is reduced.
accessibility.integrated_description: The adjacent transcript names checkpoint identity, threat fields, attack lanes, adaptive defense, utility, recovery, residual, and evidence boundaries.
accessibility.caption_plan: Use exact receipt-derived cues from the pinned 19-segment narration; the adjacent transcript describes each material state change.
accessibility.reduced_motion_assessment: No flash, spin, shake, or continuous camera drift; lane and evidence relations survive pause and reduced motion.

beats.narration: A learned artifact creates attack surfaces that ordinary application security does not fully own. Attackers can shape training data, perturb inference inputs, implant triggers, adapt to defenses, steal behavior through queries, infer sensitive properties, or exploit multimodal and agentic pathways while the surrounding software remains nominally secure.
beats.visual_purpose: Expose the model-specific attack surface before showing a defense.
beats.visual_action: Place one checkpoint in a vault and fan labeled attack arrows from training data, inference inputs, triggers, queries, sensitive properties, multimodal, and agentic paths around otherwise secure software.
beats.attention_target: The attack arrows that bypass ordinary software perimeter labels.
beats.composition: Checkpoint center; software shell behind; attack paths fan around it.
beats.motion_curve: Progressive reveal with a settled attack surface.
beats.camera_action: Widen from software shell to model-specific lanes.
beats.hold_purpose: Make ordinary application security visibly incomplete.
beats.evidence_boundary: Illustrative attack surface; no prevalence claim.

beats.narration: Generic access control, one robustness score, static red teaming, accuracy on clean data, or a single defense cannot characterize a model attack.
beats.visual_purpose: Reject proxy metrics that collapse distinct attack lanes.
beats.visual_action: Stack access control, robustness badge, static red team, clean accuracy, and one defense beside a red incomplete-coverage boundary.
beats.attention_target: The gap between the robustness badge and attack lanes.
beats.composition: Proxy badges left; uncovered lanes right beyond the boundary.
beats.motion_curve: Tempting stack followed by hard stop.
beats.hold_purpose: Make a single score visibly insufficient.

beats.narration: A learned model should receive security authority only through a versioned model-threat contract and attack/defense ledger that binds checkpoint identity, lifecycle stage, attacker knowledge and capability, surface, budget, objective, adaptation, transfer, observed effect, detection, mitigation, utility cost, recovery, residual, and disclosure;
beats.visual_purpose: Construct the threat contract before any attack result.
beats.visual_action: Populate an amber contract header with checkpoint, lifecycle, attacker, surface, budget, objective, adaptation, transfer, effect, detector, mitigation, utility, recovery, residual, and disclosure fields.
beats.attention_target: Identity and budget fields binding before the attack.
beats.composition: Contract fields sit above checkpoint; result badges remain absent.
beats.hold_purpose: Make threat identity prospective and versioned.
beats.evidence_boundary: A ledger schema does not prove security.

beats.narration: observed effect, detection, mitigation, utility cost, recovery, residual, and disclosure; clean accuracy, attack failure, benchmark robustness, red-team coverage, or formal certification alone establishes neither general robustness nor secure deployment.
beats.visual_purpose: Complete the outcome ledger and cross broad inference.
beats.visual_action: Add effect, detector, mitigation, utility, recovery, residual, and disclosure columns; cross clean accuracy, failed attack, benchmark, red-team, and certification badges outside.
beats.attention_target: The residual and utility columns beside crossed proxies.
beats.composition: Outcome ledger center; proxy badges outside right.
beats.camera_action: Widen to the full outcome ledger.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep attack effect and cost visible rather than just attack failure.
beats.evidence_boundary: Outcome fields are design requirements, not deployment evidence.

beats.narration: Version the threat model by model family, exact checkpoint, data and adaptation lineage, modality, lifecycle stage, access, attacker goal, knowledge, budget, and prohibited real-world effects.
beats.visual_purpose: Freeze the identity and scope of one model-threat record.
beats.visual_action: Lock family, checkpoint digest, data lineage, modality, lifecycle, access, attacker goal, knowledge, budget, and prohibited effects into a version panel.
beats.composition: Identity panel top; prohibited effects stay visibly outside.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on exact checkpoint and lifecycle.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent results from silently changing model or attacker scope.
beats.evidence_boundary: Frozen identity is necessary, not robustness evidence.

beats.narration: Maintain separate evasion, poisoning, backdoor, safeguard-bypass, extraction, inversion, transfer, adaptive, multimodal, and agentic attack lanes with complete attempt denominators.
beats.visual_purpose: Split the attack surface into countable lanes.
beats.visual_action: Create ten labeled lanes from the checkpoint, each with an attempt denominator counter and separate residual socket.
beats.attention_target: Separate denominators instead of one aggregate score.
beats.composition: Checkpoint center-left; lanes form a matrix across the frame.
beats.evidence_boundary: Separate lanes do not establish coverage completeness.

beats.narration: A concrete implementation trace makes the proposal testable. Implement a model-threat record and a safe evaluation harness over public toy or consented models.
beats.visual_purpose: Move one bounded model record into a safe harness.
beats.visual_action: Route the frozen checkpoint and threat contract into a public-toy-model harness with consent and prohibited-real-world-effects gates.
beats.attention_target: The safe harness boundary around the model.
beats.composition: Harness encloses checkpoint; attack lanes remain outside as test inputs.
beats.hold_purpose: Show a safe test surface rather than a production claim.
beats.evidence_boundary: Toy/consented harness only; no frontier transfer.

beats.narration: Include clean, random-noise, known-vulnerable, attack-aware, transfer, and adaptive controls; preserve query and tuning budgets; and report robustness with clean utility, false positives, recovery, latency, and residuals.
beats.visual_purpose: Build matched controls and a joint outcome ledger.
beats.visual_action: Populate control columns for clean, noise, known-vulnerable, attack-aware, transfer, and adaptive cases; attach query/tuning counters and utility, false-positive, recovery, latency, and residual rows.
beats.attention_target: Budget counters beside clean utility and residual rows.
beats.object_after: Matched controls with joint utility ledger
beats.composition: Controls left; utility and residual ledger right; budgets top.
beats.camera_action: Pan from controls to joint outcomes.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep denominator, utility, and cost in one frame.
beats.evidence_boundary: Ledger design does not produce a robustness estimate.

beats.narration: Maintain separate evasion, poisoning, backdoor, safeguard-bypass, extraction, inversion, transfer, adaptive, multimodal, and agentic attack lanes with complete attempt denominators.
beats.visual_purpose: Return to denominators and prevent lane collapse.
beats.visual_action: Animate each lane's numerator and denominator separately; a tempting aggregate robustness badge is crossed.
beats.composition: Ten lanes align; aggregate badge remains outside.
beats.motion_curve: Counted lane updates and hard cross.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on a lane denominator, then widen.
beats.hold_purpose: Make denominators part of the claim identity.
beats.evidence_boundary: Denominator discipline is not general coverage.

beats.narration: Evaluate defenses against adaptive attacks and matched clean utility; distinguish empirical monitoring, recovery, and bounded certificates by their actual scope.
beats.visual_purpose: Put an adaptive attacker inside the defense evaluation.
beats.visual_action: Move an attacker around a violet defense wall, then compare clean utility, attacked utility, monitoring, recovery, and certificate scopes in separate columns.
beats.attention_target: The attacker adapting around the defense.
beats.composition: Defense arena center; outcome columns right; certificate boundary dashed.
beats.motion_curve: Attacker adapts, defense holds, scopes separate.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on adaptive route, then widen to scopes.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent a static red-team result from standing in for adaptive robustness.
beats.evidence_boundary: Scope-labeled outcomes do not prove secure deployment.

beats.narration: The design can still fail. evasion training-data poisoning clean-label poisoning backdoors and trojans The correct response is to stop, narrow, quarantine, compensate, or retain an owned residual rather than narrate uncertainty away.
beats.visual_purpose: Show attack failures as explicit residual-bearing dispositions.
beats.visual_action: Route evasion, poisoning, clean-label, backdoor, and trojan tokens into stop, narrow, quarantine, compensate, and owned-residual terminals.
beats.attention_target: The residual terminal rather than a green clean badge.
beats.composition: Attack tokens left; dispositions fan right; residual owner below.
beats.hold_purpose: Make attack handling explicit rather than rhetorical.
beats.evidence_boundary: Failure taxonomy; no attack prevalence claim.

beats.narration: This chapter remains Design rationale at argument support. Its contracts, examples, tests, or local artifacts establish only their encoded scope. The chapter names proof targets rather than pretending they are already closed.
beats.visual_purpose: Place the attack-surface proposal at its support ceiling.
beats.visual_action: Stamp DESIGN RATIONALE / ARGUMENT SUPPORT over the local harness and leave proof targets open beyond a double boundary.
beats.attention_target: The support stamp and open targets.
beats.object_after: Narrow support state with open proof targets
beats.composition: Local harness left; proof targets outside right.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep the derivative from promoting the chapter claim.

beats.narration: A finite Adversarial Machine Learning and the Model Attack Surface record may hand off only when identity, authority, version, required checks, and residual ownership are present; no theorem grants empirical effectiveness or release authority.
beats.visual_purpose: Show the handoff preconditions and the no-release-authority boundary.
beats.visual_action: Populate an airlock checklist with identity, authority, version, checks, and residual owner; cross an empirical-effectiveness and release-authority exit.
beats.attention_target: Residual ownership as a required handoff field.
beats.composition: Checklist center; broad release exits right beyond red boundary.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on residual owner, then widen to blocked exits.
beats.evidence_boundary: A finite record does not grant empirical effectiveness.

beats.narration: A defense is evaluated against an attacker aware of that defense whenever the threat model permits. Clean utility, attacked utility, detection, false positives, recovery, and cost remain jointly visible.
beats.visual_purpose: Close the adaptive loop with joint metrics.
beats.visual_action: Let the attacker observe the defense and adapt; update clean/attacked utility, detection, false-positive, recovery, and cost counters together.
beats.attention_target: The cost and false-positive counters beside utility.
beats.composition: Attacker/defense arena left; six metric rows right.
beats.camera_action: Pan from attacker to metric ledger.
beats.evidence_boundary: A joint ledger is not a secure-deployment result.

beats.narration: No chapter claim or evidence state is promoted by this visual. A named mechanism is not proof of correct implementation or useful deployment. A local check or formal model does not establish real-world enforcement.
beats.visual_purpose: Prevent media from laundering attack-lab structure into security proof.
beats.visual_action: Keep the local attack ledger inside a media boundary; cross implementation, useful deployment, and real-world enforcement badges outside.
beats.attention_target: The stop bar between local evidence and broad claims.
beats.composition: Ledger left; broad claims right outside dashed boundary.
beats.hold_purpose: Make support-state discipline as visible as attack motion.

beats.narration: These boundaries matter because an explanatory derivative is useful only if it preserves the evidence ceiling of its source.
beats.visual_purpose: Align live source and visual derivative at one ceiling.
beats.visual_action: Connect the live chapter card and visual ledger with an unbroken support-state line; keep the line below any broad claim badge.
beats.composition: Source left; derivative center; shared ceiling below.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the shared support label.
beats.hold_purpose: Make evidence fidelity a visible requirement.
beats.evidence_boundary: Derivative fidelity does not increase support.

beats.narration: At most, this visual explains the chapter's design rationale at argument support; it adds no empirical, deployment, safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI result.
beats.visual_purpose: State the maximum justified inference and nonclaims.
beats.visual_action: Stamp DESIGN RATIONALE / ARGUMENT SUPPORT and fan red nonclaim arrows to empirical, deployment, safety, transfer, frontier, AGI, and ASI badges.
beats.attention_target: The narrow support stamp and nonclaim fan.
beats.composition: Support stamp center-left; nonclaims fan right outside boundary.
beats.hold_purpose: Close the chapter at its actual evidence ceiling.
beats.evidence_boundary: This beat is a nonclaim, not a result.

beats.narration: The next chapter is Privacy, Data Rights, and Information-Flow Governance. It takes responsibility for A system can preserve confidentiality and pass access checks while authorized collection, linkage, inference, memory, training, sharing, retention, or derivatives violate purpose, minimization, privacy expectations, or executable rights.
beats.visual_purpose: Hand the attack-surface ledger to privacy and rights governance.
beats.visual_action: Seal the finite model-threat receipt and open a rights/flow ledger with collection, linkage, inference, memory, training, sharing, retention, and derivative lanes beyond the airlock.
beats.attention_target: The successor rights ledger beyond the boundary.
beats.composition: Receipt left; rights ledger right beyond dashed boundary.
beats.camera_action: Widen from receipt to successor ledger.
beats.hold_purpose: Close attack-surface scope without handing off security evidence.
beats.evidence_boundary: Handoff adds no privacy or rights evidence.
